Living Well / Resource directory

Use a screen to notice the world

Start with life

What would be useful?

Return to the surroundings with a more informed question or a detail worth noticing.

The simpler starting point: Observe first and write down a question. A book, local expert, or public explanation may be enough.

Finish when: You can reconnect the resource to what you actually noticed, without treating an identification guess as certainty.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

Merlin Bird ID

Consider it when: You are curious about a bird you heard or saw.

Check first: Use suggestions as starting points and keep observation details available.

Access: Free app; email confirmation is required for continued use. Download only through the official links.

Merlin setup and access guide · Full context and source

Seek by iNaturalist

Consider it when: You want to explore a nearby organism with an identification aid.

Check first: Do not use an identification guess to decide what is edible or safe.

Access: Free app; no registration required for basic use.

Learn about Seek · Full context and source

All About Birds: bird guide

Consider it when: You prefer a reference guide before installing an app.

Check first: Compare more than one feature rather than choosing the first plausible match.

Access: The online guide is publicly readable. Separate apps, courses, or memberships have their own terms.

Explore All About Birds: bird guide · Full context and source

Stellarium Web

Consider it when: You want to explore what is in the sky.

Check first: Distinguish a visualization from current conditions and your own observations.

Access: Free browser star map. JavaScript is required; desktop and mobile products have separate offerings.

Explore Stellarium Web · Full context and source

NASA Eyes

Consider it when: You want a visual route into space-science questions.

Check first: Read the context of the simulation rather than treating it as a live view.

Access: Free browser visualizations. A supported browser and suitable graphics capability are needed.

Explore NASA Eyes · Full context and source

Science Snacks

Consider it when: You want a hands-on explanation of an ordinary phenomenon.

Check first: Follow the activity’s materials, supervision, and safety instructions.

Access: Activity instructions are free to browse; materials can cost money.

Explore Science Snacks · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Keep observation in the foreground

A resource should help answer or refine a question, not require narrating the entire outing through a device. Leave room to look, listen, and remain unsure.

Choose a suitable form of curiosity

An indoor observation, accessible description, or public explanation can be as worthwhile as an outdoor activity. No special equipment or impressive setting is required by this path.

End with the world rather than a score

You do not need a complete collection, streak, photograph, or public post. One useful question and a little more attention can be enough.

Published as a selection path, not a personal field note. Source dates and access limits belong to each resource. No paid placement or affiliation is implied.
